Type: Following his show-stealing debut in 1991 on Main Source’s track “Live at the Barbeque,” Nas delivered his debut album Illmatic to high praise in 1994. The title was derived from a Queensbridge individual named Illmatic Ice, with “illmatic” being an adjective used to describe something extraordinary. Illmatic had an all-star lineup of East Coast producers; Large Professor, DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip, and L.E.S. to provide the boom bap backdrop for Nas to display his “N.Y. State of Mind.” At 20 years old, Nas was praised for his storytelling and flow as he talked about life growing up in the Queensbridge projects.

(04/19/1994) (Illmatic officially releases)

Type: Following his 1994 debut album Illmatic, Nas returned two years later with his highly anticipated sophomore album It Was Written. Despite the praise, Illmatic slowly reached platinum status as Nas watched fellow New Yorker The Notorious B.I.G. gain bigger success the same year with his debut Ready To Die a balance of hardcore rhymes and a commercial sound courtesy of producer Puff Daddy. Manager Steve Stoute and production duo The Trackmasters were brought in to try and help Nas with that balance, but the more commercial sound and Nas introducing himself with the mafioso persona Nas Escobar led to criticism at the time

The second verse was partly reused for a Funkmaster Flex freestyle in 2005, with Nas saying "married" instead of "engaged" due to him marrying Kelis in Janurary of that year. Lastly, he reused verse 2 for the New York Shit Remix by Busta Rhymes. Type: Nas, or as it's most commonly known by, Nigger, is Nas' 9th solo studio album and released on July 7th, 2008. This album is Nas' most controversial in his entire catalogue, mostly down to its original title. Whilst various celebrities and thousands of fans defended the album's title, Nas was not allowed to release it under that name and was forced to change it to a self-titled/untitled album. The album is very political, focusing on both historic and modern day racism, as well as modern American politics, throwing shots at various politicians and TV news networks in tracks such as "Sly Fox".

The next month, an email from Nas to several Def Jam executives was leaked and showed Nas accusing them of purposefully underbudgeting the album. The album did not release on December 14th, but Nas still confirmed that it was coming. In May 2011, Nas spoke to MTV News, and stated that the project was officially dead, with the reason being that he didn't communicate with Def Jam clearly enough on what he wanted to do with the project as he was used to his independence under Sony, and that he was now focusing on his upcoming solo album, which would end up being 'Life Is Good'.
